summary: 4. The Petitioner, in compliance with the directions issued vide the Interim Order - b) In response to the objections raised by the Complainant, the Petitioner, vide its letter dated 21.4.2026, submitted its reply to the Commission and also sent the same to the Complainant by registered post and email dated 23.4.2026. However, the said letter was returned undelivered. - _c) Absence of Evidence: I am a farmer without any legal representation. My original Complaint was filed in good faith with sufficient information to identify the project, location, and nature of the grievance. Evidence in the form of land records, photographs of crop damage, and local witness_ - _g) I strongly oppose TPGTL's prayer that the Complaint be dismissed. A complaint by an ordinary rural citizen against a large infrastructure company cannot be dismissed on procedural grounds, especially when the citizen is without legal representation. The Commission is respectfully requested to adopt a citizen-friendly approach, as is consistent with its role as a public interest regulator._ - _e) Pass such other and further orders as the Commission may deem fit and just in the facts and circumstances of the present case.”_ to maintain judicial discipline and give due effect to the said interim orders. The issuance of similar directions in the present proceedings would effectively amount to circumventing the stay granted by the APTEL and would be contrary to the settled principles governing the hierarchical structure of adjudicatory authorities under the Act. _Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the Parties, the Commission reserved the matters for orders.”_ _Considering the submissions of the Appellant’s Counsel and_ **_the fact that invoices have already been raised in pursuance to the impugned order with payment date as 27.03.2026, we hereby stay the operation of the impugned order with respect to the Appellant as well as the invoices raised on it till the next date of hearing_** _._ _“The interim order, as recorded by this Tribunal on 18.03.2026, shall remain in force until further orders.”_ 21. In addition, we have considered the objection filed by Shri Sujita Kumar Jena to the present Petition, _inter alia_ , contending that the Petitioner had utilised his agricultural land and the approach road for execution of the transmission project without following the due process of law or paying compensation. He further alleged that, despite repeated representations, compensation had not been paid to him, whereas compensation had been paid to other affected landowners. The objector also alleged that, after filing the objection before the Commission, he received repeated telephone calls from the persons claiming to be associated with the Petitioner requesting him to withdraw the objection. Accordingly, he prayed for an independent inquiry into the alleged unauthorised use of his land, monitoring of the compensation process, disclosure of the identity of the persons who allegedly contacted him, and grant of appropriate reliefs. _Per contra_ , the Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 21.4.2026, has submitted that, immediately upon receipt of the objection, it had requested the objector to furnish the relevant particulars of the land, including the plot number, Khata number, and other supporting details, so as to enable verification of the alleged crop damage and the claim for compensation. The Petitioner has further submitted that, despite such request, the objector did not furnish the requisite particulars. It was also submitted that a copy of the reply had been duly served upon the objector through registered post as well as e-mail. _Thereafter_ , Shri Sujita Kumar Jena filed a further response reiterating the allegations made in his objection and contended that the Petitioner had proceeded with the construction activities without obtaining his consent or paying compensation, and that the information sought by the Petitioner was only an attempt to delay the matter instead of addressing his grievances. 22. We have considered the submissions of the objector and the Petitioner. It is noticed that the present proceedings are confined to the consideration of the Petitioner's application for the grant of a transmission licence under Sections 14, 15 and 79 (1) (e) of the Act read with the Transmission Licence Regulations. The disputes between the parties herein involve contested questions of fact relating to land use, entitlement to compensation and the alleged conduct of the representatives of the Petitioner. Therefore, the issues raised by Shri Sujita Kumar Jena fall beyond the limited scope of the present proceedings, which are concerned with examining whether the Petitioner satisfies the statutory requirements for the grant of a transmission licence under the Act and the Transmission Licence Regulations. Questions relating to the alleged unauthorised use of land, assessment of crop damage, entitlement to compensation, allegations of intimidation or coercion, and the conduct of the Petitioner's representatives require examination of disputed questions of fact and evidence, which cannot appropriately be adjudicated in proceedings for the grant of a transmission licence. Accordingly, Shri Sujita Kumar Jena can pursue such remedies as may be available to him under the applicable law before the appropriate forum or authority. 28. An extract copy of this order is to be sent to CTUIL, CEA, and BPC for information and necessary action.
title: Application under Sections 14, 15, 79(1)(e) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Transmission License and other Related Matters) Regulation, 2024 and any other amendments thereon issued from time to time by this Commission for grant of Transmission Licence to TP Gopalpur Transmission Limited (earlier known as ERES-XXXIX Power Transmission Limited).
